headline: Disney Plus tests AI-powered search for personalized recommendations
summary: The streaming giant is experimenting with a new tool that uses natural language and voice queries to suggest shows and movies tailored to your mood.
details: Disney Plus is rolling out a limited beta experiment for a new AI-powered search tool designed to offer more personalized content recommendations. This feature aims to help users find something to watch that "fits the moment," going beyond standard viewing history suggestions.

The AI test generates a customized row of shows and movies based on natural language queries, voice commands, or suggested prompts. This move aligns with Disney's broader strategy to enhance subscriber experience through increased personalization.

This initiative places Disney Plus among other major streaming services integrating AI into their search functionalities. Netflix has been testing an OpenAI-powered conversational search, and HBO Max is also experimenting with a similar feature.
Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro emphasized plans to make Disney Plus the "digital centerpiece" of the company, highlighting the importance of personalization, exclusivity, and subscriber benefits.
Beyond Disney Plus, the company is also testing an "AI-assisted" conversational search for ESPN, which provides answers, stats, and recommendations drawn from ESPN's extensive sports knowledge base.

headline_marked: [[Agentic Coding]] to transform software engineering in 5 years
headline: Agentic Coding to transform software engineering in 5 years
summary: AI agents will handle tasks like planning, reasoning, and execution, freeing developers to focus on complex problem-solving and system design.
details: Agentic coding systems are set to revolutionize software engineering over the next five years, moving beyond simple code autocompletion. These AI agents can independently plan, reason, execute tasks, and collaborate across multiple steps with minimal human intervention, behaving much like a human software engineer.

Instead of spending hours on repetitive code implementation, developers will increasingly direct multiple specialized AI agents responsible for different tasks. This shifts the value from typing code to coordinating intelligent systems, potentially reducing tasks that once took days to mere hours.

Debugging, a traditionally time-consuming aspect of software development, will also be transformed. AI agents may continuously review code while developers work, providing immediate feedback rather than waiting until the end of development. This proactive approach aims to lead to cleaner codebases and fewer production issues.

Documentation, often an afterthought, will become a continuous part of the development lifecycle. AI agents can generate explanations within the context of your codebase, creating a personalized learning experience that accelerates professional growth and shortens the learning curve for new developers.

As implementation becomes more automated, engineering skills will evolve. The ability to understand what should be built and how systems should evolve will become more valuable than simply writing code. Engineers who combine technical expertise with strong product thinking will be highly sought after.

While agentic coding offers significant benefits, it also introduces new challenges. Organizations must establish clear AI governance and review processes to maximize benefits and minimize risks. The developers who thoughtfully embrace these tools will be well-equipped for the next generation of software engineering.

This fundamental shift means developers will spend less time on repetitive coding and more time designing systems, solving complex problems, and guiding AI agents toward meaningful outcomes. It represents an opportunity for front-end and full-stack developers to deliver better software faster and focus on the creative aspects of building exceptional products.
